sections.title: Stage 9 · Grandmaster: dan level
sections.html:
Stage 9 · Grandmaster: dan level

Six lessons at dan level. Ten 3-digit numbers flashed at half a second, 4-digit sums in the head, and the biggest times and divide problems yet.

Where this stage goes

The level goal. Ten 3-digit numbers flashed at half a second, four-digit mental sums, 3 × 2 and 4 ÷ 2 in the head.

In plain words. Ten three-digit numbers flashed at half a second each. Four-digit sums in the head. Dan-level targets, the grades Japanese club kids reach after years.

How long. 4–6 months at fifteen minutes a day, six days a week.

From here the course gives drills and targets, not new lessons. The technique is finished. What grows is the size and speed of the picture.

These targets sit around the Japanese dan grades, which club children reach after years of classes. Short daily sessions beat long weekly ones on the way there. There is no promise on the date. Every child is on their own clock here.

The drills in this stage

  • Flash. Ten 3-digit numbers at 0.7 seconds, then 0.5 seconds. These speeds need the trainer for the true beat.
  • Mental. 4-digit lines, 3-digit times 2-digit, 4-digit divided by 2-digit, all in the head.
  • Listening. Ten 3-digit numbers read aloud at about one a second, exam style.

Accuracy before speed

The rule matters more here than anywhere. A child who passes 0.7 seconds at 8 of 10 is ready for 0.5. A child at 5 of 10 is guessing, and guessing at speed builds nothing. Hold each speed until it is calm. Then move.

Where this sits on the abacus ladders

Grandmaster is the dan level in our map to UCMAS, the Grand end of the Advanced module. On the flash anzan ladder, ten 3-digit numbers at 0.7 seconds is about 5th dan, Bead Score rung 16. At 0.5 seconds it is around 7th dan, rung 17. On the Times ladder, this stage covers rungs 8 and 9.

Parent lineShort and daily beats long and weekly, more than ever.

Lesson 9.1 · Flash: ten 3-digit at 0.7 s

Lesson 66 of 76. Stage 9, lesson 1 of 6. About 8 minutes. You need a grown-up to show or read the numbers. No abacus, no paper.

By the end, your child can add ten 3-digit numbers flashed at 0.7 seconds each.

The move

Ten numbers, 0.7 seconds each. The numbers are gone before they can be said in words.

There is nothing to learn here except calm. Breathe out on each number.

Lesson 9.2 · Flash: ten 3-digit at 0.5 s

Lesson 67 of 76. Stage 9, lesson 2 of 6. About 8 minutes. You need a grown-up to show or read the numbers. No abacus, no paper.

By the end, your child can add ten 3-digit numbers flashed at half a second each.

The move

Half a second. At this speed the eyes stop reading digits and start seeing bead shapes.

Do not ask what the numbers were afterwards. Only the total needs to stay on the beads.

Parent lineFilm a round on the trainer once a month, because the clips make the best record of the climb.

A grown-up shows each number for 0.5 seconds on a card, or says it at that beat, once each. Your child says only the total. This speed is hard to hit by hand. sections.title: Lesson 9.3 · Mental: 4-digit lines
sections.html:
Lesson 9.3 · Mental: 4-digit lines

Lesson 68 of 76. Stage 9, lesson 3 of 6. About 12 minutes. You need no abacus. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can add and take away five 4-digit lines in the head.

The move

Four rods in the picture. Research suggests this is near the limit of visual working memory, so it may take months to feel steady.

Five lines, mixed. If four rods will not hold, go back to 3-digit head sums for a week, then try again.

Worked example. The first two lines of a 4-digit head sum.

  • Start with .
  • + 3945. Thousands rod, plus 3: the beads are free. Hundreds rod, plus 9: take away 1, carry 1 to the left. Thousands rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Tens rod, plus 4: take away 6, carry 1 to the left. Hundreds rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Ones rod, plus 5: take away 5, carry 1 to the left. Tens rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now .
  • Read it: 9,731.
Parent lineThis page can take months, so judge it by the month, not by the day.

No abacus. Read the column, move the beads in your head, write only the answer. Pass mark: 8 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

sections.title: Lesson 9.4 · Mental: 3-digit × 2-digit

Lesson 9.4 · Mental: 3-digit × 2-digit

Lesson 69 of 76. Stage 9, lesson 4 of 6. About 12 minutes. You need no abacus. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can times a 3-digit number by a 2-digit number in the head.

The move

Six small answers on the picture. Steady rhythm. Each one lands one rod right of the one before, until the next digit of the top number starts a new row.

It is Lesson 6.6, done in the head.

Worked example. 386 × 47 on the mental beads.

  • 3 × 4 = 12. It lands on the ten thousands and thousands rods. Beads: .
  • 3 × 7 = 21. It lands on the thousands and hundreds rods. Beads: .
  • 8 × 4 = 32. It lands on the thousands and hundreds rods. Beads: .
  • 8 × 7 = 56. It lands on the hundreds and tens rods. Beads: .
  • 6 × 4 = 24. It lands on the hundreds and tens rods. Beads: .
  • 6 × 7 = 42. It lands on the tens and ones rods. Beads: .
  • Read it: 18,142.
Parent lineSay nothing during a long head problem, because one word can knock the whole picture over.

Drill

No abacus. Work each small product on the mental beads, left to right. Write only the answer. Pass mark: 8 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

sections.title: Lesson 9.5 · Mental: 4-digit ÷ 2-digit
sections.html:
Lesson 9.5 · Mental: 4-digit ÷ 2-digit

Lesson 70 of 76. Stage 9, lesson 5 of 6. About 12 minutes. You need no abacus. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can divide a 4-digit number by a 2-digit number in the head.

The move

Guess, times, take away. Twice. The guess comes from the first digits, as on the abacus.

The hard part is the times step, a 2-digit number times a guess, held while the take-away happens. Go slowly. The beads wait.

Worked example. 2,752 ÷ 32 on the mental beads.

  • Set 2,752 on the beads: .
  • 32 does not go into 2. Use the next digit too.
  • 32 does not go into 27. Use the next digit too.
  • 32 into 275: 8. Take away 2,560. Beads: . Answer so far: 8.
  • 32 into 192: 6. Take away 192. Beads: . Answer so far: 86.
  • Read it: 86.
Parent lineIf your child needs to say the guess out loud, let them, because it frees up the picture.

Drill

No abacus. Guess, multiply, take away, on the picture. Write only the answer. Pass mark: 8 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

12345
5,100 ÷ 853,380 ÷ 656,480 ÷ 812,370 ÷ 792,024 ÷ 23
678910
2,405 ÷ 654,988 ÷ 582,146 ÷ 589,215 ÷ 952,310 ÷ 77

Stuck? If the picture collapses into words, do the same sum once on the real abacus, close your eyes, and replay it.

sections.title: Lesson 9.6 · Listening: ten 3-digit numbers

Lesson 9.6 · Listening: ten 3-digit numbers

Lesson 71 of 76. Stage 9, lesson 6 of 6. About 8 minutes. You need a grown-up to read the numbers aloud. No abacus.

By the end, your child can add ten 3-digit numbers read aloud at about one a second.

The move

Numbers read aloud, about one a second. Exam-style dictation.

Say "minus" as part of the number. Keep the same beat from the first number to the last.

Parent linePractise reading the list once on your own first, so your beat stays even.

Drill

A grown-up reads each round aloud, one number about every second, once each. Your child adds on the mental beads and says only the total. Pass mark: 8 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

sections.title: The Grandmaster Boss
sections.html:
The Grandmaster Boss

Take the boss when each lesson is passed at its own speed. Part 1 maps to Lesson 9.2. Part 2 maps to 9.3. Part 3 maps to 9.4. Part 4 maps to 9.5. The flash part needs the trainer for a true half-second beat.

The printed test is Boss 9 in boss-tests.md. It has 4 parts:

  • Flash ten 3-digit at 0.5 s. 5 rounds. Need 4 of 5 in 3 minutes 20 seconds.
  • Mental 4-digit. 4 problems, five lines each. Need 3 of 4 in 5 minutes.
  • Mental 3 × 2. 4 problems. Need 3 of 4 in 5 minutes.
  • Mental 4 ÷ 2. 4 problems. Need 3 of 4 in 5 minutes.

sections.title: What the trainer adds to this stage
sections.html:
What the trainer adds to this stage

Half a second is faster than any parent can show a card. At this stage the trainer is the flash machine, and the paper pages are for the head sums, the times and divide problems, and the listening round.

The trainer also keeps the long record. By now there are many Bead Scores on the chart, and the line tells the story of the years better than any report card.
